Fourteen teams participated, once again with [[Al Ain FC|Al Ain]] as the defending champions after winning the previous two seasons. The league started on 14 September and finished on 11 May 2014 in accordance with FIFA guidelines ahead of the [[2014 World Cup]] in [[Brazil]].{{cite web |url=http://www.proleague.ae/en/news/new-season-calender.html|title=New season to kick off on 30th August with Super Cup Final |date=26 May 2013 |work=Pro League Committee |access-date=21 June 2013}} The league was previously known as the '''Pro League'''. Starting from the 2013–14 season, the name was changed to UAE Arabian Gulf League.{{cite web |url=http://www.proleague.ae/en/news/new-name.html |title=New League name announced by H.E. Mohammed Thani Murshed Al Romaithi |date=26 May 2013 |work=Pro League Committee |access-date=26 May 2013 |archive-date=24 October 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131024142752/http://proleague.ae/en/news/new-name.html |url-status=dead }} The name change has been viewed as a revival of the [[Persian Gulf naming dispute]]{{cite web|author=James M. Dorsey |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/Default.aspx?pageID=238&nid=51560 |title=MIDEAST - Gulf rivalry between Iran, UAE transferred to the football pitch |publisher=Hurriyetdailynews.com
